description: Enumerates every block weighting with independent provenance and computes E_0*S_vN of the proton|neutron cut entropy against B_AME(2H). All four overshoot by 1.69x-2.06x; none is selected or tuned. The overshoot is robust: every non-trivial vertex of the weight simplex lands in 1.79x-2.07x, and reaching AME needs 69.3% of the weight moved onto the trivial block (6,), a 6.31x concentration on the one block carrying no cut structure.
caveats: Scope (a). No weighting is selected, endorsed, or tuned; all four are computed once and reported. The two controls (classical Plancherel, uniform) are deliberately structure-poor so that agreement between them and the derived pair is informative about the CUT rather than about the weighting.

This does NOT refute an entanglement-cost contribution to binding. An overshoot of ~2x with the right sign and order of magnitude is not an exclusion, and a term entering with a coefficient or alongside others is untouched. What is established is that E_0*S_cut alone, under every weighting the framework already fixes, is about twice too large.

ONE isotope. LR branching data exists only for the deuteron, so nothing here speaks to 3H, 4He or beyond -- and a single point could not have distinguished a derivation from a coincidence even had it hit.

SHARPENS the genericity caveat of binding_cut_entropy_sign_is_forced_probe.py: a weighting CAN in principle reach anything in [0, max], but no DERIVED one does -- they cluster at ~2x and the only low region is the trivial block. The earlier caveat was right in principle and too weak in fact.
